subject: Acme procurement: next steps & PO vs card (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acmecorp.com>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@acmecorp.com>
Cc: logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme procurement: next steps & PO vs card (post-call recap)

Hi Samantha / Tom  great speaking earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: \

- Procurement path: you mentioned leaning to a standard PO + Net-30 billing, but Finance also sometimes issues via card for POC purchases. Can you confirm which you'd prefer for initial committed capacity?
- Marketplace: you were interested in whether Redwood is available via the Cloud Marketplace (could simplify procurement). You said legal would check if marketplace listing is acceptable.
- Compliance: legal asked for SOC 2 summary and sample audit logs attaching a short SOC 2 summary and I can loop in Monica from CS for a deeper tech review.

Attached: Redwood-Proposal-Acme-v1.pdf (pricing + SKUs). DocuSign link below for a quick signature if you decide to go that route: https://www.docusign.com/link/abcd-1234-reproposal

Proposed next steps: \
1) You confirm preferred billing instrument (PO vs card) and whether your PO team needs a filled PO template.
2) If PO, please share your PO template and any PO-specific fields.
3) If legal needs anything else, Monica can join a 30-min call next week.

Happy to set up a short 15-20 min sync. Thanks  

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Attachments: Redwood-Proposal-Acme-v1.pdf

From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acmecorp.com>

Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme procurement: next steps & PO vs card (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa good summary. A few answers / asks from Procurement: \

- Billing: For the initial committed purchase we'll need to go via PO (Finance requires PO for any vendor >$10k).
- PO template: attaching our standard PO template (see proc team copy). Can you fill the vendor information and send back?
- Legal: They requested Redwood's standard T&Cs and SOC 2 summary. If you can share a short SOC2 one-pager that would be helpful.
- Marketplace: We're evaluating whether buying via Marketplace simplifies approvals, but that's secondary to the PO path. Would you be able to confirm whether Redwood can accept purchases either via your Marketplace listing or via a direct PO?

I'll loop Tom (copied) who manages PO issuance and will coordinate the internal approval.

Appreciate it 
Samantha Liu
Head of Procurement | Acme Corp
Samantha.liu@acmecorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acmecorp.com>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@acmecorp.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme procurement: next steps & PO vs card (post-call recap)

Thanks Samantha glad to confirm: \

- PO: we can absolutely accept a standard PO. Please send the filled PO template and procurement email (we'll route invoices to the address you specify). Our standard payment term on the invoice is Net 30 but we're flexible to match your PO.
- Marketplace: we do have a Marketplace listing in progress; for now the fastest route is direct PO / DocuSign. If you decide Marketplace is required, we can share timeline (typically 4-6 weeks for account enablement).
- Compliance: attaching a short SOC 2 summary (Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf). Monica (cc'd) can schedule a tech call for any detailed requests (SSO, data retention, audit logs).

I've also attached a pre-filled vendor block for your PO to make it faster. If legal prefers redlines to our standard SOW, we can accept redlines as annotations and work through them; for quick PO issuance the filled template should work.

Next steps: please return the filled PO template (or let us know if you'd prefer DocuSign) and I'll coordinate legal/finance as needed.

Thanks 
Marissa

Attachments: Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf, Redwood-Vendor-Block-Filled.docx

From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@acmecorp.com>

Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme procurement: next steps & PO vs card (post-call recap)

Hi Marissa quick update from legal / procurement side: \

- Legal is reviewing the standard SOW / T&Cs you referenced. Primary ask so far is to confirm liability cap and data residency commitments. They asked if Redwood will accept our standard PO language with a Net 30 payment term; that's preferred for our Finance team.
- Marketplace: legal indicated marketplace purchases still require the same contractual review for our records, so it wouldn't bypass legal sign-off.

Where it's stuck: Legal needs the liability cap clarified (they prefer a cap of 1x fees). If Redwood can confirm acceptance or propose language, we can move to routing for signatures.

I'll circle back once I have a timeline from Legal hoping to have something early next week.

Tom Harris
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Corp
procurement@acmecorp.com

Subject: Weekly check-in: Acme PO status / anything I can unblock?

Hi Tom / Samantha checking in on status and whether there's anything we can do to help move this along. Quick recap of options we discussed: \

- Option A: Acme issues standard PO (preferred path). We'll accept the PO with Net-30 and route to our finance/legal for countersignature.
- Option B: DocuSign quick-sign (if legal approves Redwood's standard SOW) fastest to get provisioning going.
- Option C: Marketplace purchase (if procurement confirms this reduces internal approvals) but legal noted marketplace doesn't eliminate review.

Offer from our side: Monica is available this week for a 30-min legal/tech call to go through liability, data residency, and audit logs. If legal has redlines, we can do a focused session to resolve the top 3 items.

If helpful, proposed next actions: \
1) Legal confirms liability cap preference (we can accept 1x fees for initial deal or propose language).
2) Procurement returns filled PO template or confirms DocuSign path.
3) We schedule Monica call if legal requires technical details.

Appreciate any timeline happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Marissa
